description: An anatomical structure or region — for example an organ, tissue, body part, or anatomical space. Anatomy nodes come from Uberon, a multi-species (not human-only) anatomy ontology, and each node represents one distinct anatomical term with a stable identifier, a canonical name, and, where available, a text definition. Only non-obsolete terms are included. Anatomy terms are organized into two kinds of relationships that are represented as separate edge types: a subtype hierarchy (`is_a`) and structural containment (`part_of`); a single term may have several parents in either.

common_properties.name: sources
common_properties.description: The data sources that contribute this node. Always ["uberon"], since Anatomy nodes are sourced exclusively from Uberon.

common_properties.name: last_updated
common_properties.description: When this node was last created or updated.

source_contributions.scope: Every non-obsolete anatomical term in the Uberon basic anatomy ontology (OBO release). Multi-species — anatomy across organisms, not restricted to human. Terms marked obsolete in the source are excluded entirely.
source_contributions.description: Anatomical structures and regions from Uberon, a multi-species anatomy ontology. Each node is one anatomical term identified by its Uberon identifier, carrying the term's canonical name and, when the source provides one, a free-text definition.

properties.name: identifier
properties.description: Uberon identifier for the anatomical term, as a full prefixed CURIE (e.g. UBERON:0000002).

properties.name: name
properties.description: Canonical name of the anatomical structure or region, as given by Uberon.

properties.name: def
properties.description: Free-text definition of the anatomical structure.
properties.notes: Present only when the source term carries a definition; omitted otherwise.
